inputs.userGoal: If azure front door is better then use that.
subGoals: Cost-conscious: use Front Door Standard rather than Premium.
Brownfield-safe: add Front Door without recreating or modifying the existing App Service resources.
Secure cutover: validate the edge endpoint before restricting direct origin traffic.
insightsApplied: insight-001: The disabled public endpoint explains the login outage, so the existing App Service is referenced as an HTTPS origin and the origin lock is deferred until Front Door health succeeds.
insight-002: The existing F1 App Service plan is retained and explicitly referenced, with no deployable copy in the template.

resources.name: afd-opb-checkin

properties.endpoint: Globally unique name derived from subscription and resource group

reasoning.whyChosen: Provides a stable TLS edge endpoint and supports locking the App Service origin to traffic from this Front Door instance at substantially lower fixed cost than Premium.
alternativesConsidered: Azure Front Door Premium with WAF and Private Link
reasoning.tradeoffs: Standard does not include managed WAF or Private Link. The application retains its JWT authorization, exact-origin CORS, security headers, and rate limits.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The existing App Service is the only Front Door origin.

references.title: Restrict access to an Azure Front Door origin

resources.name: opb-checkin-api

reasoning.whyChosen: This is the deployed API and must be integrated as the Front Door origin.
reasoning.tradeoffs: F1 has limited resilience and does not support Private Link; upgrading is outside this cost-conscious change.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The existing application runs on the existing F1 plan.

references.title: App Service access restrictions with Front Door

reasoning.whyChosen: Retained because it already hosts the API.
reasoning.tradeoffs: No resiliency or scaling upgrade is included.

overallReasoning.summary: Add one Azure Front Door Standard profile in front of the existing API, using HTTPS-only origin traffic and an uncached catch-all route. The existing App Service and plan are referenced and never recreated.
overallReasoning.tradeoffs: Premium WAF, Private Link, Log Analytics diagnostics, multi-region origins, and an App Service tier upgrade are omitted to keep recurring cost proportionate. Origin access restrictions are deliberately a post-deployment cutover step because applying them before Front Door validation would prolong the outage.

plan.validation: The deployment is resource-group scoped and incremental. What-if must show only Microsoft.Cdn resource creation and no modification, replacement, or deletion of the existing Microsoft.Web resources.
architecturePrinciples: Least recurring cost consistent with the requested edge architecture

references.title: Azure Verified Module for CDN profiles
